svg.text: timing closes with +0.008 ns of slack
dual-port block RAM: port A 225 MHz
Clocks, resets and where data crosses between clock domains
Everything that touches DDR3 runs on the memory controller's own 225 MHz clock, so the 256-bit data path (weights, K / V, DMA) never crosses a clock domain.
The CPU runs at 150 MHz because the MicroBlaze V's pipeline does not close at 225 MHz. Only two places cross: the SmartConnect (handshaked clock converters) and the
dual-port Y / V RAMs. The RAMs need no handshake: the CPU reads a job's results only after it has seen the job's busy flag drop through the (slower) register path.
The reset button resets the DDR3 controller; its synchronized reset then resets llm_core and, through the clocking wizard and proc_sys_reset, the CPU.
